=Find the blog or news page for '{{ $('Get Vendor Record').first().json.company_name }}' (website: {{ $('Get Vendor Record').first().json.website }}).

Use the search tool to find their blog. Try queries like:
- {{ $('Get Vendor Record').first().json.company_name }} ({{ $('Get Vendor Record').first().json.website }}) blog

Return the URL of their blog LISTING page, not an individual post.

The blog might be:
- A path on their main site: example.com/blog, example.com/news, example.com/insights
- A subdomain: blog.example.com, news.example.com
- A section with a different name: /resources, /articles, /posts

Return the root of the blog (e.g. example.com/blog not example.com/blog/some-post-title).
If the blog is on a subdomain, return the subdomain root (e.g. https://blog.example.com).
If no blog exists, return null for blog_url.

=You are determining the most recent blog post date for '{{ $('Get Vendor Record').first().json.company_name }}'.

Blog URL: {{ $json.blog_url }}

I fetched several potential RSS/Atom feed URLs. Here are the responses:

{{ $json.feeds }}

Your task:
1. Check each feed response. A VALID post feed must:
   - Be RSS or Atom XML (not an HTML error page)
   - Contain actual <item> or <entry> elements with post content (not just <channel> metadata)
   - NOT be a comment feed (WordPress comment feeds have titles like "Comments on: ..." and no <item> elements)
2. If you find a valid post feed, extract the most recent <pubDate>, <published>, or <updated> date from the items.
   Also return the URL of the feed that worked as blog_rss_url.
3. If NO valid RSS/Atom feed was found among the candidates, use this blog page HTML instead to find the most recent post date:

{{ $json.html }}

   When reading HTML, scan ALL visible dates and return the MOST RECENT one.
   Do not use copyright years, footer dates, or non-post metadata.

Return blog_rss_url as the working feed URL (or null if you used HTML instead).
Return latest_post_date in YYYY-MM-DD format, or null if no date was found.
Return confidence as "high" (clear date from RSS), "medium" (date from HTML), or "low" (uncertain).
